Name: Old Keshavnagar–Kharadi Bridge weir (bandhara)
Description: Thick white froth below the weir across most of the river width; turbid grey water. Froth still across the weir on 9 Oct 2026 (seen from the Keshavnagar bank, 18.544415, 73.951621)
Source: Team field visits 29 Sep 2026 and 9 Oct 2026 (GPS Map Camera photos)
Project Link Basis: Ask the ward office (question 4); if nobody knows, the Step 5 RTI asks. Desk candidates: froth below the weir comes from untreated sewage upstream. Nearest plants: PRJ-02 Kharadi (north bank), PRJ-03 Keshavnagar (south bank), PRJ-04 old Mundhwa (upstream, rated Non-Comply)

Name: Sewage outfall near the old bridge (Kharadi bank)
Description: Concrete culvert under a tree on the Kharadi (north) bank discharging a strong flow of greenish, foamy wastewater towards the river; algae on the pipes below. About 80 m upstream of the weir (HS-01) and about 150 m from the old Kharadi sewage plant (PRJ-05)
Source: Team field visits 29 Sep 2026 and 9 Oct 2026 (GPS Map Camera photo, 9 Oct 11:17)
Project Link Basis: 9 Oct GPS puts this outfall on the Kharadi (north) bank, so the desk candidate is PRJ-02 (new Kharadi plant). It is also about 150 m from the old Kharadi plant (PRJ-05) and may be that plant's own outlet. Ask the ward office (question 4) which line this is and which plant its sewage should go to; if nobody knows, RTI-01 asks

Name: Garbage dumped on the riverbank beside the old bridge
Description: Large spread of plastic bags, clothes, sacks, wood and dark burnt-looking fibrous waste on the rocky Kharadi bank at the old bridge; still there on 9 Oct 2026
Source: Team field visits 29 Sep 2026 and 9 Oct 2026 (GPS Map Camera photo, 9 Oct 11:17)
Project Link Basis: Garbage dumping is handled by the ward office's solid waste department (see Routing Rules), not by a sewage plant

Name: Waste on the bridge walkway
Description: Plastic and cloth waste left along the bridge; waste thrown into the river from here
Project Link Basis: Garbage dumping is handled by the ward office's solid waste department (see Routing Rules), not by a sewage plant

Name: Water sample point below the weir
Description: Bottled samples were turbid and yellowish-grey, with suspended particles
Project Link Basis: Same as HS-01: water below the weir carries all upstream sewage. Ask the ward office (question 4); if nobody knows, the Step 5 RTI asks

Name: Garbage dump on Grant Road (EON Free Zone side)
Description: Large mixed-waste dump on open ground beside Grant Road: sacks, clothes, plastic, thermocol and an old office chair. More plastic waste along the dirt track by the fence towards the river (18.547723, 73.949218)
Source: Team field visit 9 Oct 2026 (GPS Map Camera photos, 11:15–11:16)
Project Link Basis: Garbage dumping is handled by the ward office's solid waste department (see Routing Rules), not by a sewage plant

Name: Open nalla near Grant Road, Kharadi
Description: Open earth channel carrying dark wastewater from an opening in the road's retaining wall, with plastic and waste along it. Grey water pools around a broken concrete chamber beside it (18.547822, 73.949192). The channel meets the river at 18.547289, 73.949595, where water hyacinth collects
Source: Team field visit 9 Oct 2026 (GPS Map Camera photos, 11:15–11:16)
Project Link Basis: Kharadi (north) bank; the nalla meets the river about 120 m upstream of HS-02. Ask the ward office (question 4) which drainage line feeds this nalla and which plant it should go to; desk candidate PRJ-02 (new Kharadi plant). If nobody knows, add it to RTI-01

Name: Rubble pushed into the river at Keshav Nagar Bridge
Description: Excavator working on a strip of rubble and soil built out into the river beside Keshav Nagar Bridge; more rubble and a concrete pipe on the far bank. Not yet known which project or contractor this is, or whether it is permitted
Source: Team field visit 9 Oct 2026 (GPS Map Camera photos from the bridge, 11:54–11:55)
Project Link Basis: Construction debris goes to the ward office (Routing Rules: Construction debris in riverbed). First find out which project the excavator belongs to and which bank it works from; if it is permitted work, record the project and permit instead of a complaint

Name: Froth line below Keshav Nagar Bridge
Description: White froth line across the river just below Keshav Nagar Bridge, where the water drops over a step (weir to confirm). Greenish water with floating plastic and hyacinth along the Kharadi bank (18.543727, 73.944289)
Source: Team field visit 9 Oct 2026 (GPS Map Camera photos from the bridge, 11:54–11:55)
Project Link Basis: Same reasoning as HS-01: froth comes from untreated sewage upstream. Upstream plants: PRJ-01 (new Mundhwa) and PRJ-04 (old Mundhwa, rated Non-Comply). Ask the ward office (question 4); if nobody knows, the RTI asks

Name: Floating plastic and garbage along the riverbank near Garware College, Khilarewadi
Description: Plastic bottles, bags and other waste floating along the stone embankment on the Deccan (Khilarewadi) bank, below the bridge near Central Mall Road. A riverbank cleanup by another group was under way nearby the same morning, with a pile of collected waste beside the path (18.510545, 73.839675). Mutha river, upstream of the study stretch
Source: Team field visit 10 Oct 2026, central Pune (GPS Map Camera photos, 8:35–8:36)
Project Link Basis: Floating and dumped waste is handled by the ward office's solid waste department (see Routing Rules), not by a sewage plant. The river is the boundary between prabhag 29 (Deccan bank) and 27 (Navi Peth bank); confirm the ward office for the Deccan bank

Name: Garbage dumped on the bank and in the river at Baba Bhide Bridge
Description: Sacks of mixed waste, plastic and cloth dumped on the rock embankment and lying in the water just below the bridge railing, with plastic floating downstream. Mats of water hyacinth along both banks between Baba Bhide Bridge and the old arch bridge beside it (18.515442, 73.844508). Mutha river, upstream of the study stretch
Source: Team field visit 10 Oct 2026, central Pune (GPS Map Camera photos, 8:39)
Project Link Basis: Dumping goes to the ward office's solid waste department; the hyacinth goes to PMC CARE and the ward health inspector (Routing Rules: Water hyacinth or weeds). The river is the boundary between prabhag 12 and 25

Name: Pipeline work in the riverbed at Dengale Bridge (Chhatrapati Shahu Setu)
Description: An excavator levelling a strip of soil and rubble built out on the riverbed beside the bridge, with a long row of large concrete pipes along the water's edge, a trench with a pipe laid in it and a diesel pump drawing water. Looks like pipeline (possibly sewer) work; which project and contractor it is, and whether the work is permitted, is not yet known (18.52421, 73.857438)
Source: Team field visit 10 Oct 2026, central Pune (GPS Map Camera photos, 8:47)
Project Link Basis: First find out which project this is (ask the ward office or the PMC Drainage Department). If it is sewer work under the Mula-Mutha (JICA) project or the AMRUT 2.0 upgrade, link that project and record the permit instead of a complaint; if not, treat it as construction debris in the riverbed

Name: Garbage on the riverbank at Old Tofkhana, Shivajinagar
Description: Plastic and household waste dumped on the steep bank below the road at Old Tofkhana, beside a concrete slab that runs into shallow water flowing fast over rocks. About 90 m from the Dengale Bridge pipeline work (HS-12)
Source: Team field visit 10 Oct 2026, central Pune (GPS Map Camera photos, 8:45)
Project Link Basis: Garbage dumping is handled by the ward office's solid waste department (see Routing Rules), not by a sewage plant. Check on the next visit whether the concrete slab carries a drain

Name: Floating waste caught at the piers of the steel bridge, Shivajinagar
Description: Thick mats of floating waste and grey scum caught against the piers of a riveted steel-girder bridge (railway bridge, to confirm), with dark, still water downstream (18.529182, 73.85928). Mutha river, upstream of the Sangam
Source: Team field visit 10 Oct 2026, central Pune (GPS Map Camera photos, 8:50)
Project Link Basis: Floating waste goes to the ward office's solid waste department. If the bridge belongs to the railways, removal at the piers may also need Central Railway (Pune division); confirm the bridge owner
